input.question: With advances in immunology and medicine, how has our immune system changed over the last hundred years?
input.ground_truth: 100 years is effectively zero time in evolutionary terms for a species with our generation time, unless the selective pressure is ludicrously high (e.g. selective breeding where all the offspring that don't have the desired trait get their necks snapped by the breeder). For more 'normal' environmental pressures, you're looking at tens of thousands of years to see something spread across the population.

Question: With advances in immunology and medicine, how has our immune system changed over the last hundred years?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a castle, and your immune system is the army that keeps you safe from tiny invaders like germs.

A hundred years ago, your castle’s army didn’t have many tools. They could fight some germs, but sometimes they got sick or tired and couldn’t protect you as well.

Now, because scientists learned a lot about these germs (that’s called immunology and medicine), your army has gotten much smarter and stronger! They have new shields (like vaccines) and better weapons (like medicines) to fight germs. This means your army can protect you from more sicknesses than before. Sometimes, the army can even fix mistakes and remember germs it has seen before, so it can beat them up faster next time.

So, your body’s army is now much better at keeping you healthy than it was a hundred years ago!
